canonical_title: Online ordering system for Feel ABAC Restaurant
committee: Asst. Prof. Dr. AnilKumar Kothalil Gopalakrishnan
abstract: Our Senior Project II is a web-based food ordering system developed for a Burmese restaurant located at Assumption University. The project aims to solve operational problems caused by the current ordering method, where customers place orders through messaging platforms such as Facebook Messenger. This manual process makes it difficult for staff to manage multiple orders, track order status, calculate prices, and coordinate delivery, which often leads to delays and communication errors. The proposed system provides a centralized platform where customers can browse the menu, customize dishes, place orders, and track their order status in real time. The platform supports highly flexible menu customization to match the nature of Burmese cuisine, where customers often choose ingredients, spice levels, and additional options. It also integrates payment through QR PromptPay and provides live order updates for both customers and restaurant staff. On the administrative side, the system includes a dashboard that allows restaurant staff to manage menu items, monitor incoming orders, update order status, and control item availability. This automation reduces manual workload, improves order accuracy, and provides better organization of restaurant operations.

canonical_title: TrustLoop: Secondhand marketplace for AU students
abstract: TrustLoop is a secure, student-exclusive online marketplace developed for Assumption University (AU) students to buy, sell, donate, and auction items within a trusted environment. The system was developed in collaboration with the administrator of the Assumption University Myanmar Students Facebook Group, where many students currently trade second-hand items through informal posts. However, platforms such as Facebook Marketplace or Facebook group posts often lack proper identity verification, which can lead to scams, fake identities, and unreliable transactions. To address this issue, TrustLoop uses Microsoft Entra ID authentication to ensure that only verified AU students can access and participate in the platform. The system includes features such as item listings, donation and request posts, auction functionality, user ratings and reviews, real-time notifications, and product management tools. TrustLoop is developed using Next.js, MongoDB Atlas, Cloudinary, and Vercel to provide a scalable and responsive web application that supports safe and convenient item exchanges within the university community.

canonical_title: Lecture sense: A notebookLM clone for lectures
committee: Asst. Prof. Dr. Anilkumar Kothalil Gopalakrishnan
abstract: students face significant challenges in managing and navigating the vast amount of lecture contents. Traditional methods of reviewing lectures often involve manual processes, such as "scrubbing" through hours of course materials to find specific information, which is inherently time-consuming and inefficient. This can lead to fragmented learning, missed deadlines, and a lack of clear visibility for instructors into student struggles. The advent of AI-driven digital solutions offers an opportunity to transform these academic proceses, making them more efficient and personalized. This project focuses on developing LectureSense, a standalone web aplication that serves as a specialized "NotebookLM clone" for lectures. The platform is designed to bridge the gap between lecture delivery and student comprehension by automatically mapping transcripts to slides and timestamps The primary objective of this platform is to enhance study efficiency and improve the instructional feedback loop by providing role-based access to tailored dashboards. For students, these dashboards facilitate searchable content, automated sumaries, and flashcard generation with direct citations to source material. For instructors, the platform clusters student questions and provides a "confusion heatmap" to identify parts of the material that require further explanation. By integrating OpenAI LLM via API and a RAG pipeline, LectureSense ensures a student-friendly system that streamlines the operational side of academic learning

abstract: Mental health among students in Thailand has become an important concern, yet it is often overlooked due to social stigma and limited access to professional support. According to the Department of Mental Health, many Thai teenagers experience high levels of stress and depression, but a significant number do not seek help because they fear being judged. In addition, students living in rural areas may have difficulty accessing mental health services. This project proposes MindNest, a mobile application designed to provide a safe and judgment-free environment where students can share their thoughts and emotions through an AI-powered chatbot. The system supports both Thai and English languages and is available 24 hours a day, allowing users to access mental health support anytime and anywhere. The chatbot is powered by artificial intelligence to provide empathetic responses, stress management guidance, and helpful coping exercises. MindNest also provides access to important mental health resources such as hotline information and calming techniques including breathing and grounding exercises. The application aims to improve accessibility to mental health support and encourage students to express their feelings in a safe and private environment. Overall, the system helps reduce barriers to seeking help and promotes better mental well-being by creating an accessible digital platform for mental health support among students in Thailand.

abstract: The rapid growth of social commerce has shifted how independent businesses, particularly bakeries, interact with their customers, heavily relying on chat applications for order placement. However, managing orders and verifying payments manually across these chat platforms introduces severe operational inefficiencies, high instances of human error, and delayed order fulfillments. This project presents BakeFlow, an integrated chat and web-based bakery management system designed to automate and streamline both customer ordering and administrative workflows. BakeFlow eliminates the bottlenecks of traditional chat commerce by bridging the gap between customer-facing chat interfaces and backend bakery operations. The system features a seamless Webview Ordering interface for customers—allowing for quick cart management and order submission without leaving their chat application—and a comprehensive Admin Dashboard tailored for efficient order tracking and direct payment slip verification. The platform was engineered using a modern, scalable technology stack, comprising a high-performance Go (Golang) backend for robust API handling, state management, and real-time processing, alongside a responsive Next.js/React frontend for an optimized user experience. BakeFlow demonstrates a significant reduction in the administrative overhead associated with manual order processing, providing bakery owners with a centralized, scalable, and user-friendly platform to manage their online sales efficiently.

canonical_title: LotusLIB - Application for scanning MTG cards
abstract: LotusLIB is a mobile application for Magic: The Gathering enthusiasts that streamlines card cataloging and collection valuation. The app performs on-device CNN inference using TensorFlow Lite to identify a card from the camera, then shows card details and lets users add it to their collection or perform other tasks. A Node.js/Express API with MongoDB Atlas powers authentication, card search with filters, profile management, file uploads, and a news feed seeded from public MTG sources. The mobile application captures frames using the device camera and detects the card region using OpenCV-based rectangle detection. The cropped image is then processed by a TensorFlow Lite model that performs on-device classification to identify the card. We document scope, related work, methodology, ROI, and a system design covering workflow, architecture, tech stack, UI/UX, and database schema. Results summarize the trained model footprint and mobile inference loop, including evaluations and matrices. We conclude with pragmatic upgrade paths: quantization, transfer learning (MobileNetV3-Small), a lightweight detector front-end, backend extensions for per-user collection sync, as well as semi-automatic Sorting System integration in the future.

abstract:
The CafeShop Ordering and Management System is developed to address common operational challenges faced by cafés, including inefficient order management, delayed communication between customers and staff, and limited access to real-time business data. Traditional café operations often rely on manual order taking and paper-based processes, which may lead to order inaccuracies, slower service, and difficulties in tracking sales and operational performance.

To solve these issues, the CafeShop system provides a digital platform that integrates customer ordering, payment processing, and administrative management into a single system. Customers can scan a QR code assigned to each table to access a digital menu through their mobile devices, browse available items, select menu variations such as sizes, and place orders directly through the system. Payments are supported through PromptPay QR code integration using the Omise payment gateway, enabling a secure and convenient cashless payment experience.

For café staff and administrators, the system provides a web-based dashboard that allows real-time monitoring and management of orders, menu items, tables, and invoices. The system utilizes WebSocket technology to deliver instant notifications when new orders are placed, allowing staff to process orders efficiently. Additionally, administrators can monitor sales data and manage operational activities through a centralized interface.

By integrating digital ordering, real-time communication, and administrative management tools, the CafeShop system improves operational efficiency, reduces manual workload, minimizes ordering errors, and enhances the overall customer service experience in café environments.

abstract:
This project presents the development of a web-based Cosmetics Business Management System designed to improve operational efficiency in sales management and administrative processes at NYK Cosmetics, a retail and wholesale cosmetics business. The system aims to reduce manual workload by providing a centralized platform that integrates sales order management, inventory tracking, customer loan monitoring, and administrative reporting.

The application enables salespersons to record customer orders digitally through a web-based system, allowing them to access the platform conveniently from tablets or web browsers. The system automatically updates inventory and transaction records in real time after each order submission. Administrators can review, adjust, and manage orders through a centralized web dashboard without relying on manual record books or scattered spreadsheets. In addition, the system includes customer loan management features that allow administrators to track outstanding balances, monitor payment histories, and maintain accurate financial records efficiently. The system also provides statistical dashboards that display sales performance by product, shop, and region, enabling better decision-making and business analysis. By implementing this system, NYK Cosmetics can reduce operational errors and improve overall business management efficiency.

The system is developed using modern web technologies including Next.js for the frontend, Nest.js for the backend, and PostgreSQL for the database, and deployed on cloud infrastructure to ensure accessibility and scalability. Overall, the proposed system establishes a centralized digital platform that enhances operational management and supports the future growth of NYK Cosmetics.

abstract:
Proper road bike fitting is essential for cycling safety, performance, and injury prevention; however, professional bike fitting systems often require specialized equipment and expert assessment, making them costly and inaccessible to many cyclists. This senior project, developed by the First Safe Point team, addresses this problem by investigating a low-cost, vision-based approach for road bike posture analysis using computer vision techniques. The proposed system utilizes MediaPipe Pose Estimation to detect cyclist body landmarks from recorded road cycling videos and computes key joint angles, including knee, hip, elbow, ankle, and back angles. These angles are evaluated against industry-standard road bike fitting ranges to provide visual posture feedback.

This report presents the initial development phase of the system, focusing on pose detection, joint angle computation, and real-time visualization, as well as the evaluation of cyclists' perceptions of the posture feedback generated by the system.

abstract:
Invisible but amplifying microplastic pollution represents a major and escalating threat not only to the global ecosystem but also to the long-term health of humanity. Resolving this environmental crisis demands both public awareness and the capacity for early intervention — goals that are severely hampered by the fact that traditional measurement techniques such as Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy are prohibitively expensive for most undergraduate laboratory settings.

This work proposes a cross-disciplinary iSTEM (integrated Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) framework designed as a full laboratory learning experience. By grounding the curriculum in the local context of Bang Saen Beach, Thailand, the framework systematically guides undergraduate Information Technology students through four sequential phases: hands-on wet-lab extraction using density separation (Phase 1), low-cost optical digitization using a USB digital microscope (Phase 2), AI model deployment and domain-adapted training (Phase 3), and a novel unified mathematical evaluation pipeline (Phase 4).

In Phase 3, students deploy and evaluate four complete neural network architectures: Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5, U-Net, and Mask R-CNN. A critical technical innovation of this study is a three-phase training sequence that includes few-shot domain adaptation specifically targeting the optical artifacts (glare, chromatic aberration) introduced by the low-cost microscope. Phase 4 introduces a post-processing pipeline that converts all model outputs — whether bounding boxes or pixel-level segmentation masks — into a standardized bounding-box representation, enabling fair cross-architectural comparison. A novel environmental metric, the Contamination Percentage (Cp), is derived from the unified output to translate raw AI detections into a measurable, physically interpretable scale of local contamination severity.

All four architectures achieved statistically significant detection performance above random chance under a right-tailed one-sample z-test at α = 0.05. Mask R-CNN achieved the best overall result with an F1-score of 0.8287, instance accuracy of 70.75%, and the highest statistical significance (z = 3.7627, p = 0.000084). Faster R-CNN placed second (F1 = 0.7918), followed by YOLOv5 (F1 = 0.7830) and U-Net (F1 = 0.7423). The results demonstrate that deep learning tools can be successfully deployed in resource-constrained undergraduate classrooms, and that the iSTEM framework provides an accessible, reproducible, and scalable tool for educators to meaningfully embed the global microplastic health crisis into computer science and engineering curricula.

abstract: CodeFix is a Python-based debugging practice platform. It is for beginner programmers to take care of syntax errors and variable errors by doing debugging practice. These days, most beginner programmers spend a lot of their time finding syntax errors and variable errors. This often reduces learning efficiency and negatively affects confidence in coding. To reduce the occurrence of those errors, CodeFix will be practiced with three modes: (i) normal mode, (ii) game mode. In normal mode, students can practice Python debugging problems at easy, medium, and hard levels. CodeFix lets learners test broken code, understand the error messages, and follow gradually stronger hints. They can figure out the correct fix by themselves. By practicing like this, they don't need to use most of their time finding syntax errors and variable errors. In game mode, there is a short storyline game, and users need to solve some problems to win. Game mode is designed to attract people to be interested in programming and not to be afraid of coding languages. CodeFix aims to build confidence, improve error-analysis skills, and strengthen exam performance for beginner programmers. To evaluate the effectiveness of CodeFix, beginner programmers participate in debugging practice sessions using the platform, and their performance is analyzed in terms of error-fixing accuracy, time spent on debugging tasks, and hints used. The expected outcome of this project is to help students develop systematic debugging habits, reduce the time spent finding syntax errors and variable errors, and prepare learners for real-world coding tasks.

canonical_title: Simplification of Technical Documentation in STEM Education for Neurodivergent Individuals
advisor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Dobri Atanassov Batovski
abstract: Technical documentation and user interfaces (UI) in STEM are often designed for a general audience. They are usually filled with dense text, long sentences, and jargon, which can introduce learning difficulties, especially for students with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder or dyslexia. This preliminary study evaluated the effectiveness of a constraint-based prompting framework that was based on standard accessibility guidelines and rules to simplify both documentation and UI microcopy while largely preserving important details from the original content using a large language model. We collected two pilot datasets for this study and simplified the contents using the Gemini-3-Pro-Preview Model. Simplified and original content pairs were evaluated using computed readability/fidelity metrics and a pilot survey measuring perceived understanding and mental effort using Likert scale questions. Readability metrics showed improvements with high retention of technical terms and numeric/format token preservation. For the pilot survey, improvements on results of ease, mental demand, and self-reported main idea understanding of reading passages were significant. Additionally, participants selected optimized UI microcopy more frequently over original versions. Significant benefits for the targeted screened population over the control group, however, were not established in this pilot, motivating further studies on personalization, baseline comparisons, and larger-scale validations.

canonical_title: Automation Aspects of Spin-Locked Magnetic Levitation
advisor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Dobri Atanassov Batovski
abstract: This project presents the design and implementation of an machine learning magnetic levitation system capable of manipulating lightweight objects through transparent barriers without the use of electromagnets or direct physical contact. The system leverages the repulsive and attractive forces between two permanent magnets one spinning rotor magnet above and one freely suspended floater magnet below it to achieve stable levitation and controlled spatial movement of a target object. A sole purpose of this work is the integration of a real-time pipeline powered by machine learning to close the control loop. Developing a machine learning aspects using Reinforcement learning method on monitors the position, and stability of the levitated object, feeding this data into a trained model that dynamically adjusts the speed, direction, and vertical position of the spinning magnet. This feedback mechanism enables the system to perform precision levitation including lateral translation, rotational control, and active stabilization against instability all without human intervention. Unlike conventional magnetic levitation approaches that rely on electromagnetic coils and complex power electronics, this system is purely passive on the levitation side, reducing hardware complexity while demonstrating that intelligent software control of the spin can compensate for the unstable nature of permanent-magnet equilibria. The result is a compact, low-power, and mechanically simple platform with potential applications in contactless object handling, laboratory automation, educational demonstrations, and manipulation in sealed or sterile environments. This work demonstrates that the combination of Magnetostatics, mechanics and modern machine learning techniques which can allow new ways of contactless manipulation.

abstract: Docker has become one of the most important tools in modern software development for building, deploying, and managing applications in containerized environments. However, many developers face difficulties when writing Dockerfiles manually, remembering complex syntax, managing multi-stage builds, and executing Docker commands correctly. This project introduces DockForge, a Visual Studio Code extension designed to simplify Dockerfile creation and container management through a graphical user interface. DockForge provides an intuitive development environment that allows developers to visually construct Dockerfiles, validate them in real time, test builds with live logs, and run containers directly from within the VS Code interface. The system integrates Docker CLI functionality, Docker Hub search capabilities, and real-time validation tools into a unified workflow. By reducing complexity and improving usability, DockForge enhances developer productivity and lowers the barrier to adopting Docker in modern software development workflows.

abstract: Cloud infrastructure plays an important role in modern software development. Developers often need servers, databases, and other resources in order to build and test applications. However, in many organizations the process of requesting these resources is slow because developers must wait for operations teams to manually provision them. This delay can slow down development and reduce team productivity. Orchestronic is an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) designed to simplify and automate the process of cloud resource provisioning. The platform allows developers to request infrastructure resources through a self-service interface while maintaining approval and control by project managers and IT personnel. The Orchestronic platform has been developed over multiple senior project phases. In Senior Project 1 (Semester 2/2024), the first team introduced the initial concept and built the foundation of the system, focusing on basic cloud resource provisioning and core system architecture. In Senior Project 2 (Semester 1/2025), the second team improved the system by expanding the platform's capabilities, improving the user interface, and adding support for additional cloud resources and workflow management. This project represents Part 3 of the Orchestronic platform, developed during Senior Project 2 (Semester 2/2025). The goal of this phase is to further enhance the platform by improving automation, expanding infrastructure capabilities, and integrating additional development tools that support modern cloud-based workflows. By continuing the development of Orchestronic, this project aims to create a more complete Internal Developer Platform that helps organizations reduce manual infrastructure management, improve collaboration between development and operations teams, and accelerate software development processes.
